claims.text: Removing cobalt from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi increases lattice distortion in FeNiCrMn.
Removing cobalt alters the stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrMn.
The cobalt-removal-induced changes elevate the activation barrier for dislocation glide.
Low temperatures and high strain rates favor dislocation slip and twinning in the Co-free alloy.
Elevated temperatures or lower strain rates produce earlier dynamic recovery and partial recrystallization in the Co-free alloy than in CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed Co-free FeNiCrMn starting material is a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution with negligible secondary phases.
Mechanical behavior will be compared over 25–900 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-3 s^-1.
Using identical processing and heat treatment for the two alloys will control microstructural differences.
Enhanced lattice distortion changes dislocation-core structures and the relative mobilities of edge and screw dislocations.
Changes in edge and screw dislocation mobility influence the onset of recovery and twinning.
An increased glide activation energy causes more pronounced strain-rate sensitivity at low temperatures.
At higher temperatures or lower strain rates, thermally activated recovery and partial recrystallization become dominant and enhance ductility.
The Co-free alloy will have higher yield strength than CoCrFeMnNi under low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions.
The Co-free alloy will exhibit a more rapid reduction in yield strength with increasing temperature than CoCrFeMnNi.
The Co-free alloy will exhibit a more rapid reduction in yield strength with decreasing strain rate than CoCrFeMnNi.
The Co-free alloy will transition earlier from dislocation-dominated deformation to recovery/twinning-dominated deformation than CoCrFeMnNi.
The baseline is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi tested under the same temperature and strain-rate conditions.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to homogenized, single-phase alloys over 25–900 °C and 10^-4–10^-3 s^-1 and may fail in precipitate-containing or multiphase materials.
TEM measurements of dislocations, twins, subgrains, and recrystallized fraction can distinguish the proposed deformation mechanisms.

Failure to observe either significantly higher low-temperature/high-rate yield strength or an earlier recovery-associated ductility transition in FeNiCrMn relative to CoCrFeMnNi would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Twinning is first assigned to low-temperature/high-strain-rate deformation, whereas the predicted outcome groups twinning with recovery as the later, recovery-dominated regime expected at higher temperature or lower strain rate.
